Avogadro guide · Minecraft 1.12.2 / Cleanroom

Choose an example

Choose a chemical below to see its rendered model and the code that builds it. Copy a complete recipe into your mod or script, then register it to make it available in Minecraft. Avogadro does not install these examples automatically.

Example language Your choice applies across the guides.
Java imports 
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.molecule.*;
// Client code only:
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.export.*;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;

The chemical examples

Tip These are authored or SMILES-generated display models. Their coordinates are schematic, not optimized conformations or evidence of measured physical properties. Hydrogens are included; the sodium chloride cell has no covalent bonds.

Register individual models from SMILES

Register the example collection

Pass the definitions you want from the examples above. Build each definition with its own ID, then publish them together. In GroovyScript, pass the builders directly to the script batch so the registrations follow the script’s reload cycle.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static MoleculeBatch catalog() {
    var batch = new MoleculeBatch();
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:water")
        .name("Water")
        .structure(water())
        .items("minecraft:water_bucket")
        .fluids("water")
        .generateItem(true));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:methanol")
        .name("Methanol")
        .structure(methanol()));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:ethanol")
        .name("Ethanol")
        .smiles("CCO"));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:aspirin")
        .name("Aspirin")
        .smiles("CC(=O)OC1=CC=CC=C1C(=O)O"));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:caffeine")
        .name("Caffeine")
        .smiles("CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C"));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:crown")
        .name("18-crown-6")
        .smiles("C1COCCOCCOCCOCCOCCO1"));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:ammonia")
        .name("Ammonia")
        .structure(ammonia()
            .fragment()));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:peg")
        .name("Polyethylene glycol")
        .polymer(peg()));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:rubber")
        .name("Sulfur-linked polyisoprene")
        .polymerNetwork(rubber()));
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:salt")
        .name("Sodium chloride")
        .structure(saltBasis())
        .crystalCell(new CrystalCell(5.64, 5.64, 5.64, 90, 90, 90))
        .formula("NaCl"));
    return batch;
}

public static StructureFragment water() {
    // All atoms are explicit: StructureBuilder does not add hydrogens.
    return new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("O",
            0,
            0,
            0)
        .atom("H",
            .7586,
            .5043,
            0)
        .atom("H",
            -.7586,
            .5043,
            0)
        .bond(0, 1)
        .bond(0, 2)
        .attachment("oxygen", 0)
        .atomConfiguration(0, new AtomicConfiguration(8, 8, 0, List.of(2, 6)))
        .atomConfiguration(1, new AtomicConfiguration(1, 0, 0, List.of(1)))
        .atomConfiguration(2, new AtomicConfiguration(1, 0, 0, List.of(1)))
        .build();
}

public static StructureFragment hydroxyl() {
    // An open O site for assembly; this piece alone is not an alcohol.
    return new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("O",
            1.43,
            0,
            0)
        .atom("H",
            1.8,
            .85,
            0)
        .bond(0,
            1)
        .attachment("oxygen",
            0)
        .build();
}

public static StructureFragment methanol() {
    // Fragment positions already line up. link() only adds the O–C bond.
    return StructureAssembly.builder()
        .part("methyl", methyl())
        .part("hydroxyl", hydroxyl())
        .link("methyl/carbon",
            "hydroxyl/oxygen",
            BondType.SINGLE)
        .build()
        .build(); // recipe first, then finite geometry
}

public static StructureEditResult ammonia() {
    // Change O to N and add the third hydrogen: H2O -> NH3 as a graph edit.
    // This demonstrates authoring; it does not simulate a reaction.
    var editor = water()
        .edit()
        .replaceAtom(0, "N")
        .moveAtom(0, 0, 0, .25);
    int hydrogen = editor.addAtom("H", 0, -.85, -.35);
    return editor.setBond(0, hydrogen, BondType.SINGLE)
        .build();
}

public static PolymerDefinition peg() {
    // HO–(CH2–CH2–O)n–H. Caps supply both terminal hydrogens and the extra oxygen.
    var unit = new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("C",
            0,
            0,
            0)
        .atom("C",
            1.5,
            0,
            0)
        .atom("O",
            2.9,
            .2,
            0)
        .atom("H",
            -.3,
            .8,
            .65)
        .atom("H",
            -.3,
            -.8,
            -.65)
        .atom("H",
            1.7,
            .8,
            -.65)
        .atom("H",
            1.7,
            -.8,
            .65)
        .bond(0,
            1)
        .bond(1,
            2)
        .bond(0,
            3)
        .bond(0,
            4)
        .bond(1,
            5)
        .bond(1,
            6)
        .attachment("head",
            0)
        .attachment("tail", 2)
        .build();
    var head = new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("O",
            -1.4,
            -.2,
            0)
        .atom("H",
            -2.2,
            .2,
            0)
        .bond(0,
            1)
        .attachment("end",
            0)
        .build();
    var tail = new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("H", 3.8, .2, 0)
        .attachment("end", 0)
        .build();
    return PolymerDefinition.usingAttachments(unit,
        "head",
        "tail",
        new PolymerDefinition.Vector(4.3,
            0,
            0),
        BondType.SINGLE,
        PolymerDefinition.Cap.usingAttachment(head,
            "end",
            BondType.SINGLE),
        PolymerDefinition.Cap.usingAttachment(tail, "end", BondType.SINGLE), 4);
}

public static PolymerNetworkDefinition rubber() {
    var sulfur = new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("S",
            4.2,
            2.2,
            0)
        .attachment("left",
            0)
        .attachment("right",
            0)
        .build();
    var hydrogens = new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("H",
            4.2,
            1.4,
            0)
        .atom("H",
            4.2,
            3.0,
            0)
        .attachment("left",
            0)
        .attachment("right", 1)
        .build();
    var pair = StructureAssembly.builder()
        .part("left", rubberUnit())
        .part("right", rubberUnit()
            .translate(0, 3.6, 0))
        .choice("bridge", "sulfur_bridge", "bridgeChance",
            StructureAssembly.builder()
            .part("connector", sulfur)
            .build(),
            StructureAssembly.builder()
            .part("connector", hydrogens)
            .build())
        .link("left/cross", "bridge/connector/left", BondType.SINGLE)
        .link("right/cross", "bridge/connector/right", BondType.SINGLE)
        .build();
    var head = new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("H",
            -1,
            0,
            0)
        .atom("H",
            -1,
            3.6,
            0)
        .attachment("left",
            0)
        .attachment("right", 1)
        .build();
    var tail = new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("H",
            5.2,
            .4,
            0)
        .atom("H",
            5.2,
            4,
            0)
        .attachment("left",
            0)
        .attachment("right", 1)
        .build();
    var assembly = StructureAssembly.builder()
        .repeat("pairs", pair, "length", StructureAssembly.translation(5.7, 0, 0))
        .neighbor("left/tail", "left/head", 1, BondType.SINGLE)
        .neighbor("right/tail", "right/head", 1, BondType.SINGLE)
        .endGroups(StructureAssembly.builder()
            .part("cap", head)
            .build(),
            StructureAssembly.builder()
            .part("cap", tail)
            .build())
        .link("pairs/head/cap/left", "pairs[first]/left/head", BondType.SINGLE)
        .link("pairs/head/cap/right", "pairs[first]/right/head", BondType.SINGLE)
        .link("pairs[last]/left/tail", "pairs/tail/cap/left", BondType.SINGLE)
        .link("pairs[last]/right/tail", "pairs/tail/cap/right", BondType.SINGLE)
        .build();
    return new PolymerNetworkDefinition(List.of(PolymerNetworkDefinition.Parameter.count("length",
        1,
        16,
        4),
        PolymerNetworkDefinition.Parameter.probability("bridgeChance",
            .5)),
            assembly,
            42L);
}

public static StructureFragment saltBasis() {
    // Conventional rock-salt cell, a = 5.64 Å. No covalent Na–Cl bonds.
    var basis = new StructureBuilder();
    double a = 5.64;
    double[][] sodium = {
        {
            0, 0, 0
        }, {
            0, .5, .5
        }, {
                .5, 0, .5
        }, {
                .5, .5, 0
        }
    };
    double[][] chlorine = {
        {
                .5, .5, .5
        }, {
                .5, 0, 0
        }, {
            0, .5, 0
        }, {
            0, 0, .5
        }
    };
    for (double[] p : sodium) {
        int atom = basis.addAtom("Na", p[0] * a, p[1] * a, p[2] * a);
        basis.atomConfiguration(atom,
            new AtomicConfiguration(11,
            12,
            1,
            List.of(2,
            8)));
    }
    for (double[] p : chlorine) {
        int atom = basis.addAtom("Cl", p[0] * a, p[1] * a, p[2] * a);
        basis.atomConfiguration(atom,
            new AtomicConfiguration(17,
            18,
            -1,
            List.of(2,
            8,
            8)));
    }
    return basis.build();
}

public static StructureFragment saltBasis() {
    // Conventional rock-salt cell, a = 5.64 Å. No covalent Na–Cl bonds.
    var basis = new StructureBuilder();
    double a = 5.64;
    double[][] sodium = [[0, 0, 0], [0, .5, .5], [.5, 0, .5], [.5, .5, 0]] as double[][];
    double[][] chlorine = [[.5, .5, .5], [.5, 0, 0], [0, .5, 0], [0, 0, .5]] as double[][];
    for (double[] p : sodium) {
        int atom = basis.addAtom("Na", p[0] * a, p[1] * a, p[2] * a);
        basis.atomConfiguration(atom,
            new AtomicConfiguration(11,
            12,
            1,
            List.of(2,
            8)));
    }
    for (double[] p : chlorine) {
        int atom = basis.addAtom("Cl", p[0] * a, p[1] * a, p[2] * a);
        basis.atomConfiguration(atom,
            new AtomicConfiguration(17,
            18,
            -1,
            List.of(2,
            8,
            8)));
    }
    return basis.build();
}
This operation runs in code. JSON stores definitions and recipes; it cannot call this method or handle events. Select or for the working example.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static CompletableFuture<MoleculeView> registerCatalog() {
    // Replaces this owner's contribution only. Other owners are untouched.
    return AvogadroApi.owner("guide")
        .replace(catalog());
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described.

    ],
    bonds: [[0, 1], [0, 2]],
    items: ['minecraft:water_bucket'],

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or setting Arguments What it does
AvogadroApi.builder(id) Namespaced molecule ID Give each copied model an ID controlled by your addon.
batch.register(builder) Molecule definition or builder Add the model and its matching rules to the batch.
owner(name).replace(batch) Owner name; complete batch Publish the catalogue as one owned replacement set.

When you finish: A builder creates a model but does not add it to the game. Java registrations use a name, called an owner, to group the definitions your mod controls; choose your mod ID. A RegistrationJob lets you cancel pending work or remove its installed set later. JSON and Groovy registrations use their file or script loading rules instead. Keep drawing and exports in client code.
